themes.name: Agentic AI in research
themes.description: This theme covers AI agents designed to perform specific research tasks, from data analysis to content generation, often acting autonomously or semi-autonomously.

themes.name: AI coding assistants
themes.description: Articles focused on AI tools that aid developers in writing, debugging, and understanding code, accelerating the software development lifecycle.

themes.name: AI summarization
themes.description: Content related to AI's ability to condense large amounts of text, such as research papers, meeting transcripts, or articles, into concise summaries.

themes.name: AI research tools comparison
themes.description: This theme includes articles that evaluate, compare, and rank various AI tools available for research and related professional tasks.

themes.name: Synthetic users
themes.description: Articles discussing the creation and use of artificial or simulated user profiles for research, testing, or data generation purposes.

themes.name: AI-powered data analysis
themes.description: This theme focuses on AI's application in analyzing large datasets to identify patterns, trends, and insights for business or research purposes.

themes.name: AI survey tools
themes.description: Content related to AI-powered platforms and techniques for designing, distributing, and analyzing surveys more effectively.

themes.name: AI chatbot research
themes.description: Articles exploring the use, impact, and research surrounding AI-powered chatbots, including their conversational capabilities and potential effects on users.

themes.name: AI design & research
themes.description: This theme covers the intersection of AI with design principles and user research methodologies, including AI's role in ideation and prototyping.

themes.name: AI workforce impact
themes.description: Articles that examine how AI is changing the job market, including job displacement, skill requirements, and the creation of new roles.

note: Themes identified by analyzing articles from curated sources, Google News, HackerNews, and DEV.to this month.
